plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks negative profit; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $15, I'll bid $15.

This is a second-price auction (Vickrey auction), where the winner pays the second-highest bid rather than their own bid. In this format, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: if I bid exactly my value, I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest competing bid, and I pay that second-highest amount, guaranteeing non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if others bid high; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions unnecessarily. With no repeated learning needed (single round), truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction. The dominant strategy in second-price auctions is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others do. This is because: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value ensures I only win when profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks negative profit; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding is optimal.
